html:
A port city on the Geba estuary, fortified by the Portuguese from 1687 as a slave-trading post, which became the capital of Portuguese Guinea in the early 1940s and of independent Guinea-Bissau.

It grew slowly behind the fort of Sao Jose. As capital it drew people from all the country's peoples, and its port workers began the open fight for independence after the Pidjiguiti massacre of 1959. Fighting in the civil war of 1998 and 1999 damaged much of the city. Most of the country's cashew crop is shipped from it. See also Cacheu.
